mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates strengthening labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months with PAYEMS growth exceeding 100k, or the Rank IC falls below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals an active monetary tightening cycle that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of months with FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year period.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous expansion in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals robust consumer demand that lifts corporate revenues and stock prices, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months where both HOUST and RSAFS rise by at least 1% month-over-month, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles, a rising federal funds rate compresses equity valuations through higher discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of months classified as monetary tightening cycles, or the Rank IC for the regime-specific signal is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates early-stage economic expansion that boosts consumer confidence and corporate investment, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months with HOUST growth exceeding 0.5%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.05 over a 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4.0%, it indicates a tight labor market that supports wage growth and consumer spending, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months with UNRATE < 4.0%, or the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year period.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent growth in industrial production (INDPRO) and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a synchronized expansion in manufacturing and labor markets, which drives corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months where both INDPRO and PAYEMS rise by at least 0.5% month-over-month, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In early recovery phases following a recession, a rising industrial production (INDPRO) indicates manufacturing sector recovery that boosts corporate profits and stock prices, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months classified as early recovery phases with INDPRO growth exceeding 0.3%, or the Rank IC for the regime-specific signal is below 0.03.
